direction.name: The page is the object
direction.idea: Find the printed or physical artefact that already exists in the subject's world and build the page as that thing. A wedding site is the invitation card. A restaurant is its menu. A conference is the ticket; a record is its sleeve; a shop is the receipt or the swing tag; an archive is a stack of tabbed folders; a course is the syllabus sheet. The artefact supplies everything a template would otherwise invent: its proportions, its typographic manners, its way of grouping information. Visitors recognise the object instantly, which is why these pages feel specific.
direction.composition: The first screen shows the artefact as a single filled panel (paper colour on a contrasting ground) centred or offset, with believable proportions: a card at 5:7, a ticket at about 2.2:1 with a notch cut by `clip-path`, a menu as a tall sheet. All primary content lives on it, set the way that object is set: centred and symmetrical for an invitation, in tidy aligned columns for a menu or ticket. The ground behind is a flat colour or one full-bleed photograph. As the page continues, each section is another piece of the same stationery: a second card, a tear-off stub, a folded panel, always filled shapes with real edges (straight, notched, scalloped, perforated by a dotted `border` of round dots at 4px or more), never outlined boxes. The footer is the back of the object.
direction.typography: Take the manners of the artefact: a bookish serif with small caps avoided, or a blunt condensed face for tickets and posters. Sizes stay within what print would use relative to the panel; the name is large on the panel, details are small and exact.
direction.colour: Paper and ink plus the ground the paper sits on. Two or three flat colours in total, like a two-colour print job.
direction.imagery: Optional. One photograph behind the object, or small photographs placed on it like tipped-in plates. The object itself is the image.
direction.richness: Recognition. The shaped edges, the print-like alignment and the limited inks make a familiar object out of plain HTML.
direction.pitfalls: Choose an artefact that truly belongs to the subject, or it becomes costume. Shape the edges with fills and `clip-path`; an outlined rectangle with a thin border is not an object. Keep text sizes readable on a phone, where the object becomes full width with its shaped edge kept at top and bottom.

hero.name: Card over a dim room
hero.blueprint: A full-bleed, low-key photograph of the room fills the viewport, darkened with `filter: brightness(0.7)` so it reads as atmosphere. Centred over it is one square-cornered panel in a flat warm tone taken from the photograph: columns 4–10, about 55% of the width and 62% of the height, a filled programme card with 32px padding. Along its top edge the three words of the title are spread to the left, centre and right in bold condensed capitals at clamp(28px, 2.5vw, 38px); that line is the headline. Under it sit two left-aligned blocks in the same face and size, line-height 1.0: the facts (date, time, place) as three short lines, then one supporting sentence held to 30ch. Along the card's bottom edge: a credit at left in 14px, the single action as a solid rectangular button in the centre, one text link at right. There is no navigation outside the card. The card is `position: sticky`: as the page scrolls it shrinks with `transform: scale` toward the bottom-left corner and stays there as a ticket-sized stub while photographs of differing sizes pass on a flat ground.
hero.mobile: The photograph fills 100svh and the card sits centred at full width minus 16px margins, 70svh tall. The title words stack as a two-line heading at 9vw at the card's top-left. The facts and the supporting sentence follow at 5.2vw in the condensed face. The action button spans the card's bottom edge. On scroll the card shrinks to a 120px stub pinned bottom-left.
hero.headline: The event or venue name, three words at most and up to about 8 characters each, spread across the card's top edge; two lines on a phone.

type.note: A grotesk with visible stroke contrast and slightly irregular curves, so headings look drawn rather than engineered. Suits reports, consultancies and design-led software that want warmth without a serif.

palette.name: Walnut and tan
palette.note: Dark walnut holds the opening and the close with bone type, and the middle of the page may turn to flat tan around honey-lit photographs. There is no bright accent: tan is the fill for the one button on walnut.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: The printed menu sheet
sections.blueprint: The list is one tall sheet of paper. A filled paper-colour panel 640px wide sits centred, or offset to columns 7–12, on a contrasting flat ground or a full-bleed photograph, with square corners and its top and bottom edges cut into shallow scallops by `clip-path` or an SVG `mask`. Inside, 64px padding and a centred, symmetrical setting like a printed card: the venue or section name at 40–48px, a one-line note at 15px, then three or four groups 56px apart. Each group opens with its name at 22px, centred. Items follow at 17px with 16px between them: the dish or service at the left of a 420px measure, the price at the right with tabular figures, and a one-line description at 14px in the soft ink under the name. Alignment alone links name and price; there are no leaders. The sheet ends with the opening hours as two centred lines. Holds 12–24 items.
sections.mobile: The sheet spans the screen with 10px of ground showing at each side and 28px padding; the scalloped edges stay at top and bottom. The measure is the full inner width and prices stay right-aligned. Group names at 20px, items at 16px.

sections.name: Photo tiles with label strips
sections.blueprint: Four columns with 12px gaps; every tile is a photograph with a filled label strip attached directly beneath it, the two forming one object like a print with its swing tag. The photograph is 1:1 or 4:5 with square corners. The strip is the same width, 84–96px tall with 12px padding, and holds two or three rows of text at 12–13px in the text face with tabular figures: row one spreads four short values evenly across the width with `justify-content: space-between`; row two puts a date at the left end and a time or place at the right end; row three names the maker or model. Strip and text colours change per tile through four palette pairs (dark on bright, bright on dark), so a uniform grid looks varied. Rows of tiles are 28px apart. A two- or three-word heading at 32px sits top-left, 40px above the grid. Holds 8–16 tiles.
sections.mobile: Two columns with 8px gaps. Strips keep two rows only: the four values wrap to two per row, and the date and place line is dropped. Text stays at 12px. The heading sits above at 24px. Colour pairs keep rotating so adjacent tiles never match.

sections.name: The reply card
sections.blueprint: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page. On a dark or strongly coloured flat field about 80svh tall, a paper-coloured panel 44vw wide with 7:5 proportions sits in columns 6–12, rotated two degrees, with its lower edge hanging 60px past the section's bottom so the section crops it. On the card, with 48px padding, everything is centred the way stationery is: a heading of two to four words at 32px, one or two lines at 17px, then the action as a solid bar across the card's full inner width, 56px tall, in the ink colour with paper-coloured text. Columns 1–4 hold only a short paragraph at 20–24px in the field's light ink, bottom-aligned 64px above the edge. The card is a plain filled rectangle with square corners and no outline; its rotation and crop make it an object.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 20px. The card follows at 90% width, tilted one degree, centred, its bottom edge still cropped by the section. Heading at 24px, lines at 16px, and the action bar 52px tall across the full inner width of the card.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: Sarah & Matt Wedding
references.idea: The site is the invitation: a letterpress-style card rendered as a physical object opens the page, and its ornaments, rules and small typographic parts become the components for everything after it.
references.hero: A flat blush-pink field fills the viewport. Top-left sits a gold filigree monogram about 120px square; three plain nav links are centred on the same line; a solid gold rectangular RSVP button sits top-right. Below, centred, a portrait invitation card half the viewport wide starts 200px down and is cropped by the bottom edge, with a soft halo shadow and a debossed border with scalloped inner corners. On the card: the two names in a large italic swash serif, staggered left and right against two ornamental roundels, separated by hairline rules carrying tiny wide-tracked caps for date and time.
references.type: Card names in a high-contrast italic serif with swash capitals (drawn in canvas); section titles in a light roman serif around 5vw; Instrument Sans 18px for body and nav; Spezia Extended in tiny tracked caps for dates and addresses. Three clear tiers.
references.colour: #e9c4be #faf7f5 #0d0b0a #241c22 #9b7948 #4f5660 — Each section takes its own field: blush pink hero, warm cream story, dark plum venue details, black footer. Gold is reserved for ornament and the RSVP button; a coral button appears once on dark.
references.imagery: A canvas-rendered paper card with emboss and grain; a warm, grainy golden-field landscape as a full-bleed band behind it; candid couple snapshots in equal portrait cards with rounded corners; night venue photos overlapping at two sizes.
references.layout: Outer margins of about 50px. The hero is centred; the story is a horizontally scrolling row of text-above-photo columns; the details section splits roughly 45/55 between text and overlapping photos. Large vertical gaps separate sections, each on its own colour field.

sections.description: A story timeline. A small sans heading sits at the left margin with two outlined circular arrow buttons at the right. Under it runs a full-width ruler of fine vertical tick marks acting as a scrubber. Below, a horizontally scrolling row of columns about 280px wide: each has a one-line bold caption, three lines of small grey text, a large gap, then a portrait photo with 12px rounded corners. Columns bleed off both edges; one photo is black and white.

A cream field with a single light serif title at roughly 5vw on the left margin and a three-line small sans paragraph pushed to the far-right column on the same baseline, leaving the middle empty. Below, the date in medium sans introduces a row of large light-serif times divided by vertical hairlines, with a dark rounded image card starting in the right half.

On a dark plum field, split in two. Left 45%: small sans labels for arrival and ceremony, an outlined box holding venue, street and city in tiny tracked extended caps separated by slashes, then a five-row accordion with hairline dividers and chevrons, then a coral button beside a text link. Right 55%: a tall night photo of the venue facade bleeding off the top, with a smaller square photo overlapping its lower-right corner.

A band of grainy rose-brown texture, then black. A dim monogram at left, a four-link column at centre, and at right the date, boxed address and time lines repeated from the invitation in tracked extended caps with hairlines. The couple's names run across the full width at about 22vw in the italic swash serif, filled with a blue-gold glitter texture and cropped by the bottom edge.

steal: Make a real-world object (an invitation, a ticket, a label) the hero and reuse its small typographic parts, such as a boxed address line with slashes, as recurring components down the page.
Repeat the hero lettering in the footer at full-bleed scale with a material texture fill, cropped by the bottom edge.
Place a section title at the left margin and its short paragraph in the far-right column on the same baseline, leaving the centre empty.

references.name: The Deep End
references.idea: The whole site is one invitation card floating over ambient footage, which shrinks into a pinned corner ticket as scattered stills scroll past.
references.hero: Full-bleed, dim, amber-toned video of a listening room: a modular synth and speaker at top, a person lying on a silk cushion in soft focus. Centred over it is a square-cornered panel about 55% of the viewport wide and 62% tall, a blurred brown-to-taupe wash. Inside, the three words of the title are spread along the top edge at left, centre and right in bold condensed caps. A small line-diagram logo sits below. Two left-aligned text blocks at 2.5vw in the same heavy condensed face, tightly leaded: five lines of event details, four of description. Bottom edge: credits left, an RSVP box centre, a small link right. No navigation.
references.type: PP Neue York extra-bold condensed is the only face, used at essentially one size, 36px, in white with very tight leading; credits drop to about 12px. Mixed case with occasional all-caps lines and a raised underlined ordinal. Hierarchy comes from spacing and position alone.
references.colour: #2b2216 #bda38b #c8874a #f1f1e9 #181818 — Warm browns and ambers lifted straight from the footage: dark walnut video, a taupe translucent card, then a flat tan page with honey-lit photos. White type only; no accent colour.
references.imagery: Low-light cinematic video and stills of people lying with eyes closed, shallow focus, amber backlight, wood panelling. Square-cornered and at very different sizes, from small thumbnails to near full-height frames, placed off-grid on flat tan.
references.layout: After the full-bleed opener the page becomes a flat tan field where photos are placed irregularly, one small at left, one mid-size near centre, one tall at right, with wide gaps. The invitation card stays pinned top-left. About four screens, no headings or sections.

sections.description: Flat tan background. Images sit at irregular positions and scales with no shared grid: a small landscape still about 14% wide near the left edge, a mid-sized one about 16% wide lower and nearer the centre, then a large portrait frame about 26% wide and a full viewport tall near the right. One video frame returns nearly full-bleed between them. No captions; all text lives in the pinned card, which partly overlaps the images.

On scroll the invitation panel collapses to a card pinned in the top-left corner, about half the viewport wide and 22% tall, flush with the edges. It keeps the three-word title spread along its top, the logo, five lines of date and address, and the RSVP box centred on its bottom edge. Its fill is semi-transparent taupe with a blurred dark vignette, so photos passing beneath tint it.

steal: Spread the words of a short title to the left, centre and right of a card's top edge so the name becomes its frame.
Set every line of an invitation in one heavy condensed face at one size and let line breaks and gaps create the hierarchy.
Shrink the hero card into a pinned corner ticket that keeps date, place and the RSVP button visible for the whole scroll.

references.name: Cursor Compile
references.idea: The event name drawn as seven looping one-line curves in seven colours, more signature than logotype, on an otherwise whisper-quiet off-white page whose images are re-rendered as rows of coloured characters.
references.hero: Warm off-white field with no header or navigation. Starting about 23% down, a line-drawn wordmark spans from 8% to 92% of the width and about 29% of the height: each letter is a single 2px stroke looping like a Lissajous figure, each in a different colour (orange, green, olive, lilac, black, brown, blue), overlapping its neighbours. Directly beneath, two 14px captions, one flush left in ink and one flush right in grey. After a gap of about 20% of the viewport, three equal columns sit at the bottom, each topped by a hairline: an 18px statement, a grey 14px paragraph, and an email field over a full-width near-black rectangular button.
references.type: The only large lettering is the drawn wordmark. All real text is CursorGothic regular in two sizes, 18px and 14px (the largest text on the page is 1.8vw), sentence case, with hierarchy made by ink versus mid-grey rather than by size or weight.
references.colour: #edece8 #26251e #f07a1f #2e9e3a #2f6bf0 #9b8ff0 — Warm paper ground with near-black and grey text. The wordmark's colours return one at a time as the single ink of each character-rendered image (lilac, teal, green, orange). Event photos are dark and warm.
references.imagery: Two kinds: landmarks and speaker portraits redrawn as rows of tiny characters in one saturated colour on a tint of the same colour; and dark, warm documentary event photos. All are square-cornered rectangles in strict rows.
references.layout: About 7% side margins on a three-column grid. Each section has a small two-line heading at left (title in ink, subtitle in grey), then a row or carousel of equal tiles with one-line captions beneath. Very large vertical gaps between sections; a denser photo grid near the end.

sections.description: Tour dates as a three-column grid of 3:2 tiles. Each tile is a city landmark rendered entirely in rows of small characters in one colour on a pale tint of that colour: lilac, teal, green, orange. Under each tile, one caption line: city name in ink, date in grey straight after it, and a status word flush right. A fourth tile wraps alone to the left of a second row, leaving two columns empty.

Session recordings as stacked carousels. A small heading and grey subtitle, then per stage a tiny label at left with two arrow glyphs at far right and a row of 16:9 dark photo tiles, two full tiles visible and a third cropped by the margin. Each tile has a small white event tag in its bottom-left corner. Caption beneath: speaker name in ink followed by the talk title in grey on the same line.

Speaker row: one-line heading at left, arrows at right, then four near-square portrait tiles with 8px gaps, each a face drawn in horizontal rows of characters in one colour on its tint (orange, green, lilac, teal). Some tiles show only plain stripes with the face barely emerging, so portraits appear to resolve from lines as they load or on hover.

After a three-column photo grid with mixed landscape and portrait crops and 8px gaps, the page ends on an empty off-white screen holding one centred sentence at 18px and a small dark pill button beneath it. There are no footer columns, links or legal rows.

steal: Draw the name as one continuous thin looping stroke per letter, each in a different colour, and let it be the only large element on the page.
Keep all text at two small sizes and build hierarchy from ink versus grey on the same line (name in ink, detail in grey right after it).
Re-render photographs as rows of tiny characters in a single saturated colour on a tint of that colour, one colour per tile.
